payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x satisfies the Kunz inequalities for multiplicity m, namely: for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Then N(m,g), the number of numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g, is equal to the cardinality of K_{m,g}.

result_payload.proof_summary: I cannot give a rigorous self-contained proof from the provided material alone. The lemma is essentially the Kunz-coordinate characterization/counting statement for numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g, but the necessary definitions and prior facts are not supplied here: in particular, how a numerical semigroup of multiplicity m is encoded by a tuple (x_1,...,x_{m-1}), why the stated inequalities are exactly the closure conditions, and why the genus equals x_1+...+x_{m-1}. Without those ingredients, the equality N(m,g)=|K_{m,g}| cannot be derived rigorously from the current context.
